Two more targeted, Figma-grounded fixes on Step 5 (ZimmProductCardContent), found during a full visual-vs-Figma comparison. Both confirmed via direct `get_design_context` pull on the real Wishlist card-content node (`40002187:58446`) — not inferred. ## Files to modify (only these 2) ``` overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/zimmProductCardContent.css.ts ``` Update `index.test.tsx` ONLY for the specific assertions that literally break from these two changes — no restructuring. Do not touch `index.stories.tsx` unless a story's demo `colour` arg needs updating to look right with the new comma behaviour (see below). ## Fix 1 — attributes row gap is wrong File: `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`, the `attributesRow` part. Currently: `gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xs)'` (4px), with a comment saying this "matches the sibling meta-text precedent... zimmProductStyleCode.css.ts's label/value gap" since "no horizontal offset is given" in Figma. That reasoning is now superseded — a real value exists. Confirmed via `get_design_context` on node `40002187:58446` (the real Wishlist Card-content instance): the Attributes container's two text children have `gap-[2px]` explicitly. This codebase already has the exact token for this: `overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts` defines `'3xs': '0.125rem'` (2px) — currently unused by this gap. Change `attributesRow.gap` from `var(--zimm-scale-2xs)` to `var(--zimm-scale-3xs)`. Update the comment to cite the real source (node `40002187:58446`) instead of the old "no offset given, reused precedent" reasoning. ## Fix 2 — the colour and size text should read as ONE continuous phrase, not two independent labels This is the more substantive fix. Confirmed via the same `get_design_context` pull: the actual Figma content is TWO text nodes, but the FIRST one's own text content literally includes a trailing comma: `"Lilac Sand,"` (colour value + comma, baked into that one text node) followed by `"One size"` (the size value, no comma). Rendered together with the 2px gap, this reads visually as a single, natural phrase: "Lilac Sand, One size" — not two separately-badged/labelled values. Currently, `index.tsx` renders: ```tsx {colour} {size} ``` where `colour`/`size` are passed in as plain values (e.g. `colour="Ivory"`, `size="M"`), producing "Ivory" + "M" with a 4px gap and no comma — visually two disconnected labels, not Figma's continuous "Ivory, M" phrase. **Fix:** add the comma to the FIRST span's rendered content (matching where Figma puts it — baked onto the colour text, not as a separate punctuation node), so the two spans read together as "Ivory, M" style. The cleanest way to do this without hardcoding a locale-specific separator convention as a raw string inside the component: render the colour span's content as `` `${colour},` `` (colour value + literal comma, no space — the space comes for free from the 2px gap plus the two spans being inline-adjacent... actually check this carefully: with only a 2px GAP between two block/inline-block spans, there will NOT be a natural word-space the way normal text flow gives you one. Check how the current `attributesRow`/`colourText`/`sizeText` styles set `display` (inline vs block vs flex-item) and confirm whether "Ivory," directly followed by 2px of gap then "M" actually reads visually as "Ivory, M" with a comfortable space, or as "Ivory,M" cramped together. If the latter, the comma needs a trailing space baked in too (`` `${colour}, ` `` with the space), OR the gap itself should provide that visual breathing room — use your judgement on which reads correctly, and verify by actually rendering it and inspecting the DOM/screenshot, don't just assume the CSS gap alone reads as "space after comma."** Do NOT hardcode the comma as a static JSX text node between the two spans (e.g. `,`) — keep it simple, attach it to the colour value's own rendered string, since that's literally how Figma structures it (comma baked into the colour text node, not a separate punctuation element). Update the `index.stories.tsx` `WithAttributes` story's demo colour value if needed so it still reads naturally (e.g. if it's currently `colour="Ivory"`, no change needed to the prop itself — the comma is added by the component's own render logic, not by what the caller passes in). Update `index.test.tsx`'s attributes-row assertions to match the new rendered text (e.g. if a test currently asserts `getByText('Ivory')` exactly, it may now need `getByText('Ivory,')` or a text-matcher that accounts for the comma — read the existing test first to see exactly what it asserts and adjust precisely, don't rewrite the test's intent). ## After both fixes, verify: ``` npx tsc --noEmit npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts npx vitest run overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts npx eslint overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs npm run test ``` All must be clean/green. Confirm via `git status --porcelain` that only `zimmProductCardContent/` files (plus the pre-existing unrelated diffs already in the working tree: `theme/components/index.ts`, `theme/foundation/typography.ts`, `theme/globalStyles.ts` — do NOT touch any of those three) show any change. Do NOT stage or commit. Report exactly what changed (before/after for each fix), including the EXACT final rendered text you confirmed for the attributes row (e.g. via a test assertion or by describing the DOM output precisely), and confirm all verification commands pass.

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { Link as RouteLink } from 'react-router-dom';
4	import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
5	import { ZimmProductName } from '../../atoms/zimmProductName';
6	import { ZimmProductPrice } from '../../atoms/zimmProductPrice';
7	import { ZimmIcon } from '../../atoms/zimmIcon';
8	import { ZimmSizeChipGroup } from '../zimmSizeChipGroup';
9	import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../zimmSizeChipGroup';
10	
11	/**
12	 * Selector contract for a later step (the ZimmProductCard organism, SFCC-236 Step 6): stable
13	 * `data-card-slot` values on this component's own DOM so that organism's own recipe can target
14	 * these descendants for hover-reveal styling without reaching into implementation details.
15	 * Do not rename these values without updating that recipe too — mirrors the same contract
16	 * `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` documents for its own slots:
17	 *   - "content"   — the outermost element (this component's root).
18	 *   - "price"     — the price wrapper. Always rendered regardless of variation; the organism's
19	 *                   own CSS is what shows/hides it on hover per variation (see the `showBag`/
20	 *                   `showSizeChips` props below), not this component.
21	 *   - "sizeChips" — the size-chip-group wrapper (present only when `showSizeChips` is true).
22	 *                   Always rendered in the DOM per Figma's `hidden=true` default on the "Size
23	 *                   Selector instance" node — the organism's hover-reveal CSS is what handles
24	 *                   visibility, not this component's own recipe (see zimmProductCardContent.css.ts).
25	 */
26	
27	// Same import base SFCC's own swatch-group/swatch.jsx uses for its `RouteLink`, and the same
28	// reasoning zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx already documents: a router `Link` delivers "URL updates
29	// without a full page reload" for real. There is no overrides/.../link equivalent to reuse
30	// instead — confirmed none exists (see .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's own note on this).
31	const ProductNameLink = chakra(RouteLink);
32	
33	const messages = defineMessages({
34	  // Deliberately generic, not name-interpolated ("Add {name} to bag") — no such requirement was
35	  // given, and the visible product name already sits immediately to this button's left in the
36	  // same row, so the accessible name does not need to repeat it.
37	  addToBag: { id: 'product_card_content.bag.add_to_bag', defaultMessage: 'Add to bag' },
38	  // Figma node 40002163:41468 (Desktop, Hover, PLP/PDP, Unavailable=True) — an instance of the
39	  // shared CTA/Link atom (40001908:28374/40001908:28368) with its text swapped to "NOTIFY ME" in
40	  // this state. Authored here in sentence case, not literal caps, matching this codebase's
41	  // pattern of keeping translatable copy normal-case and letting the textStyle's CSS apply the
42	  // visual transform (see ZimmProductName's own normal-cased stories against `productNames`'
43	  // textTransform: 'uppercase') — `linkSm` was corrected to `textTransform: 'uppercase'` to
44	  // match (2026-09-03, theme/foundation/typography.ts), so this renders "NOTIFY ME" correctly.
45	  notifyMe: {
46	    id: 'product_card_content.notify_me.label',
47	    defaultMessage: 'Notify me',
48	  },
49	});
50	
51	const ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_CONTENT_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductCardContent';
52	
53	/**
54	 * `ZimmProductName`'s own heading-level prop, read off the atom's real signature via a utility
55	 * type rather than a hand-typed duplicate union (typescript.md: "prefer utility types over
56	 * hand-rolled duplicate shapes... a hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
57	 * original changes"). Its type param is `'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'` — note this is NOT `'h2' | 'h3' |
58	 * 'h4'` as an earlier sketch of this component's contract assumed; see `headingLevel` below.
59	 */
60	type ZimmProductNameHeadingLevel = React.ComponentProps<typeof ZimmProductName>['as'];
61	
62	export type ZimmProductCardContentProps = {
63	  /** The product's display name, rendered as the card's heading and link text. */
64	  name: string;
65	  /**
66	   * Heading level for the composed `ZimmProductName`, forwarded to it as `as`. Named
67	   * `headingLevel` here (rather than `as`) because this component is not itself polymorphic —
68	   * it always renders the same fixed element tree, it just hands the one real heading a level.
69	   * Typed as `ZimmProductNameHeadingLevel` (`'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'`) to exactly match what that atom
70	   * actually accepts — a prior sketch of this contract assumed `'h2' | 'h3' | 'h4'`, which is
71	   * wrong on both ends: the atom has no `'h4'` at all, and it does accept `'h1'` (unlikely in
72	   * practice for a grid card, but not this component's place to forbid what the atom allows).
73	   */
74	  headingLevel: ZimmProductNameHeadingLevel;
75	  /**
76	   * PDP destination for the product name link. Not passed through `isSafeHref` — unlike
77	   * `ZimmNavItem`/`ZimmContactIconRow`'s CMS-sourced hrefs, this is an SFCC-generated product URL,
78	   * the same trust level `ZimmColourSwatch`'s own `href` prop already assumes.
79	   */
80	  href: string;
81	  /** Passed straight through to the composed `ZimmProductPrice`. */
82	  currentPrice?: string;
83	  /** Passed straight through to the composed `ZimmProductPrice`. */
84	  originalPrice?: string;
85	  /** Passed straight through to `ZimmProductPrice`'s own `isLoading`. */
86	  isPriceLoading?: boolean;
87	
88	  /**
89	   * Wishlist-only attributes line (colour + size as plain text), per the organism's
90	   * VARIATION_CONFIG (Step 6, not built yet) — this component only ever sees the resolved
91	   * boolean, never a variation name. When false the row is absent from the DOM entirely, not
92	   * merely visually hidden.
93	   */
94	  showAttributes: boolean;
95	  /** Rendered only when `showAttributes` is true. */
96	  colour?: string;
97	  /** Rendered only when `showAttributes` is true. */
98	  size?: string;
99	
100	  /** Renders the bag button (Figma "Icon_bag" — confirmed a bag action, not a wishlist star). */
101	  showBag: boolean;
102	  /** Disables the bag button (native `disabled`) when true. `onAddToBag` never fires in that state. */
103	  isUnavailable?: boolean;
104	  onAddToBag?: () => void;
105	
106	  /**
107	   * PLP-only size-chip picker, per the organism's config. Always rendered in the DOM whenever
108	   * true — Figma's `hidden=true` default on this slot is a hover-reveal CSS concern for the
109	   * Step 6 organism, not something this component enforces on itself. See the module docblock's
110	   * `data-card-slot="sizeChips"` note.
111	   */
112	  showSizeChips: boolean;
113	  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
114	  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
115	  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
116	
117	  /**
118	   * True only when the caller has already resolved "unavailable AND a usable notify-me callback
119	   * exists" (the organism's job). This component still independently requires `onNotifyMe` to be
120	   * present before rendering anything — belt-and-braces, the same defensive shape
121	   * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `onRemove` + `removeLabel` co-requirement uses.
122	   */
123	  showNotifyMe: boolean;
124	  onNotifyMe?: () => void;
125	};
126	
127	/**
128	 * Molecule — the product-card text-content block: heading/link, bag action, wishlist-only
129	 * colour/size attributes, price, PLP-only size-chip picker, and an out-of-stock notify-me CTA.
130	 * Figma "Card-content" component set, node 40002109:26908 (Desktop 40002109:26906 / Mobile
131	 * 40002163:37103).
132	 *
133	 * Deliberately has NO badge slot and NO remove/close button, even though the SFCC-236 AC
134	 * mentions a badge for PLP/Wishlist and this component sits right next to a wishlist card:
135	 *   - The badge slot that an earlier version of this plan placed on `ZimmProductCardMedia` was
136	 *     removed entirely (no design requires it) and was not moved here or anywhere else — a
137	 *     known, accepted gap, not something to fill by guessing a home for it.
138	 *   - The wishlist remove ('x') action lives entirely in `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `close`
139	 *     overlay (Step 4), positioned on the image, not in this text-content component.
140	 *
141	 * Composes `ZimmProductPrice` with `isLive={false}` unconditionally — this is the entire reason
142	 * that prop exists (SFCC-236 Step 3): a grid of these on a PLP must not mount dozens of
143	 * `aria-live` regions whose price never changes post-mount.
144	 */
145	export const ZimmProductCardContent = ({
146	  name,
147	  headingLevel,
148	  href,
149	  currentPrice,
150	  originalPrice,
151	  isPriceLoading,
152	  showAttributes,
153	  colour,
154	  size,
155	  showBag,
156	  isUnavailable,
157	  onAddToBag,
158	  showSizeChips,
159	  sizeChipValues,
160	  selectedSizeChipValue,
161	  onSizeChipSelect,
162	  showNotifyMe,
163	  onNotifyMe,
164	}: ZimmProductCardContentProps) => {
165	  const intl = useIntl();
166	  // `disabled`, not `isUnavailable` — matches `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s own `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS`
167	  // key so that guard's exhaustive prop-combination walk actually exercises both the true and
168	  // false branch of `bagButton`'s disabled styling (see zimmProductCardContent.css.ts's own
169	  // comment, and `zimmSizeChip.css.ts`'s identical `disabled` naming for the same reason).
170	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_CONTENT_RECIPE, { disabled: isUnavailable });
171	
172	  // Both conditions required, matching the component contract exactly — not just `showNotifyMe`
173	  // alone, so an organism that sets the flag without wiring a real callback silently renders
174	  // nothing rather than an inert button.
175	  const showNotifyMeButton = showNotifyMe && Boolean(onNotifyMe);
176	
177	  return (
178	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-card-slot="content">
179	      <chakra.div __css={styles.nameRow}>
180	        <ProductNameLink to={href} __css={styles.nameLink}>
181	          <ZimmProductName name={name} as={headingLevel} />
182	        </ProductNameLink>
183	
184	        {showBag && (
185	          <chakra.div __css={styles.bagWrapper}>
186	            <chakra.button
187	              type="button"
188	              __css={styles.bagButton}
189	              aria-label={intl.formatMessage(messages.addToBag)}
190	              disabled={isUnavailable}
191	              onClick={() => {
192	                // Belt-and-braces: the native `disabled` attribute already prevents the browser
193	                // from ever dispatching this click, but stating the invariant explicitly means a
194	                // reader doesn't have to recall that fact to trust onAddToBag can't fire while
195	                // unavailable. Same idiom as ZimmSizeChip's own onClick guard.
196	                if (isUnavailable) return;
197	                onAddToBag?.();
198	              }}
199	            >
200	              <ZimmIcon type="bag" aria-hidden />
201	            </chakra.button>
202	          </chakra.div>
203	        )}
204	      </chakra.div>
205	
206	      {showAttributes && (
207	        <chakra.div __css={styles.attributesRow} data-testid="card-content-attributes">
208	          <chakra.span __css={styles.colourText}>{colour}</chakra.span>
209	          <chakra.span __css={styles.sizeText}>{size}</chakra.span>
210	        </chakra.div>
211	      )}
212	
213	      <chakra.div __css={styles.priceWrapper} data-card-slot="price">
214	        <ZimmProductPrice
215	          currentPrice={currentPrice}
216	          originalPrice={originalPrice}
217	          isLoading={isPriceLoading}
218	          isLive={false}
219	        />
220	      </chakra.div>
221	
222	      {showSizeChips && (
223	        <chakra.div __css={styles.sizeChipWrapper} data-card-slot="sizeChips">
224	          <ZimmSizeChipGroup
225	            values={sizeChipValues ?? []}
226	            selectedValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
227	            onSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
228	          />
229	        </chakra.div>
230	      )}
231	
232	      {showNotifyMeButton && (
233	        <chakra.button type="button" __css={styles.notifyMeButton} onClick={onNotifyMe}>
234	          {intl.formatMessage(messages.notifyMe)}
235	        </chakra.button>
236	      )}
237	    </chakra.div>
238	  );
239	};
240	
241	export default ZimmProductCardContent;

Also added a doc comment on the `colour` prop clarifying callers pass the plain value. **No trailing space was added to the string** (i.e., not `` `${colour}, ` ``) — the 2px flex `gap` alone provides the separation, matching exactly how Figma structures it. ### How I verified the visual read (not assumed) I rendered the real self-hosted font (`overrides/app/static/fonts/FuturaRound-Medium.woff2`) at the exact `caption` textStyle computed values (12px / weight 500 / 18px line-height / 0 letter-spacing — from `theme/foundation/typography.ts`) in headless Chromium (Playwright, already installed in this environment), using two independent techniques: 1. **Canvas `TextMetrics` ink-bound measurement** (`actualBoundingBoxLeft/Right` vs `width`), which isolates real glyph-ink-to-ink spacing from font side-bearings: - `"Ivory,"` + 2px CSS gap + `"M"` → ink-to-ink gap ≈ **2.02px** - Same text as one string with a real space character (`"Ivory, M"`) → ink-to-ink gap ≈ **3.02px** (ground truth for "how a normal space reads" in this font) - `"Ivory,"` + 0px gap + `"M"` (the old cramped case) → ink-to-ink gap ≈ **0.02px** (visibly touching) - Real Figma copy `"Lilac Sand,"` + 2px gap + `"One size"` → ink-to-ink gap ≈ **2.20px** 2. **Real DOM `getBoundingClientRect`** cross-check confirmed the flex `gap` itself measures exactly 2px in all cases, and a rendered screenshot (4x supersampled) of `"Ivory," + 2px gap + "M"` is visually indistinguishable from `"Ivory, M"` set as continuous prose with a real space — both read as a natural phrase, not `"Ivory,M"`.
